artifacts.summary: 7-phase, 8-hour plan covering all three parts: Phase 1 wires the reap pair into /todo (acceptance-critical, Wave 1, no dependencies), Phase 2 widens the reaper's globs to all four naming generations, Phase 3 untracks the retired-convention orphan and documents Check B's coverage limit, Phases 4-6 relocate both singletons into specs/.orchestration/ (writers, 19th runtime-file class member, ~121 test-fixture references across 7 suites, 9 prose sites), Phase 7 redeploys, runs the full gate set, and sweeps the live litter.

next_steps: Run /implement 51 to execute the plan. Phase 1 is the acceptance-critical deliverable and depends on nothing, so it must land and commit before the relocation phases start. Phases 4-6 are the designated drop candidates if effort must be cut.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan relocates a runtime file that scripts derive by path-string concatenation (e.g. mt_state_file="$(dirname "$STATE_FILE")/.orchestrator-multi-state-${session_id}.json"), the writer/reader count understates the blast radius by roughly two orders of magnitude: test suites hardcode the same literal fixture paths for their own assertions. In agent-system's core extension, 4 writer/reader sites corresponded to ~121 literal references across 7 test files (92 in one suite alone). Before scoping a path relocation, grep the test tree separately from the source tree and count -- a research pass that enumerates only writers/readers/docs will miss the largest single category of churn.
